His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. They are the worst of creation.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, they are the best of creation.﴾ ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾

God's judgment in this verse is the eternal abiding of the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists (who are the worshippers of idols) in the Fire, and that they are the worst of creation. "Al-bariyyah" (creation) is the whole of creation, because Allah Most High created them (bara'ahum), that is, brought them into existence after non-existence. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and al-A'raj read "al-bari'ah" with a hamza, from "bara'a". The rest of the readers and the majority read "al-barriyyah" with a doubled yā' and without a hamza, by way of facilitation (al-tashil). The analogical form would be with the hamza, but this is among the words whose hamza has been dropped, like "al-nabiyy" and "al-dhurriyyah". Some grammarians read "al-barriyyah" as derived from "al-bara", which means dust; but this derivation makes the hamza an error and a mistake, and it is not acceptable.

"Those who believed and did righteous deeds" are conditions that encompass all of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and whoever believed in his prophet from the earlier nations. The majority of people read "khayr" (best). Some readers of Makkah read "khiyar" with an alif. A hadith has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "he recited this verse: ﴿They are the best of the creation (al-bari'ah)﴾, then said to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him): 'You, O 'Ali, and your followers'," mentioned by al-Tabari. And in a hadith: "A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'O best of creation!' He said to him: 'That is Ibrahim (peace be upon him).'"

(p-665) As for His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens﴾, there is an omitted modifier in it, its estimated form being: the dwelling of gardens, or the entry into gardens. "Adn" means staying and permanence; one says "'adana bi-l-mawd'i" (he stayed at the place). From it comes "al-ma'din" (mine/mineral source), because it is a firm, stable origin. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Jannat 'Adn: the middle (buṭnān) of Paradise," that is, its center.

As for His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾, it has been said: this is in this world. So His pleasure with them is the signs of His mercy and forgiveness that He manifests upon them, and their pleasure with Him is their contentment with everything He has apportioned to them of all provisions and decrees. Some of the righteous said: the pleasure of servants with Allah Most High is their contentment with what He sends down of His rulings, and His pleasure with them is that He grants them success in being pleased with Him. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: Being pleased with Allah Most High is the removal of aversion from the heart until there is nothing but joy and delight. Sari al-Saqati said: If you are not pleased with Allah, how can you seek that He be pleased with you?

It has also been said: this is in the Hereafter. So their pleasure with Him is their contentment with the blessings He has bestowed upon them, and His pleasure with them is what has been related: that "Allah Most High says to the people of Paradise: 'Are you pleased with what I have given you?' They say: 'Yes, our Lord; and how would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone else among the worlds?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than all that I have given you? My good pleasure; I will never be displeased with you again.'"

Allah Most High singled out, in mention, those who fear (Him), because fear (khashyah) is the head of every blessing, the one that forbids sins and commands what is right.

The commentary on Surah [lam yakun] is complete, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
